data.narrative:
Poseidon Aerospace is a seed-stage space and aerospace company founded by David Zagaynov, Parker Tenney, and Isaac Baumstark, having raised $12M+ to date. The valuation exercise draws from a comp universe of 5 public peers (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private companies including SpaceX, Sierra Space, and Planet Labs operating in the same sector.

Of the three valuation methods tested, only stage-progression proved applicable. This method anchors to the company's $12M total raised as a proxy base value and applies a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of seed-to-next-stage progressions, yielding an implied valuation of $30M. The peer-median approach was not viable due to insufficient same-stage and adjacent-stage comparables within the narrow space and aerospace universe—while 11 same-sector peers exist, filtering by stage and tier produced zero datapoints. Public-comp anchoring using the sector's 23.9x P/S median was similarly inapplicable without disclosed revenue figures.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $26M to $34M, with a median of $30M. This range reflects conservative and upside applications of the stage-progression logic. The primary uncertainty is the absence of a robust peer-median benchmark and lack of revenue disclosure, both of which constrain triangulation depth. A subsequent funding round with fuller disclosure or achievement of operational milestones would substantially improve valuation granularity.
